doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Founding of the Jazz Foundation in 1989
summary: Panken lays out the founding by Herbert Storfer, Cy Blank, Billy Taylor and others from the former Jazz Museum.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Let’s step back for a minute.
The year Street News started, 1989, is also the year, I believe, the Jazz Foundation of America was started.
Isn’t that interesting. I had forgotten about that.

It’s very interesting. Let’s give the history of the Jazz Foundation of America. You give the history, but I’ll just get this started. It was founded in 1989 by a cosmetics executive who had gone into executive searcher by the name of Herbert Storfer. He had a friend from Columbia Business School who was in the retail business named Seymour “Cy” Blank. Dr. Billy Taylor, the great jazz pianist and educator and overall spirit. Phoebe Jacobs and Ann Ruckert. Three of them had been involved in the formation of the Jazz Museum in the 1970s, which then was forced to close in 1977, and a lot of their memorabilia went to the Schomberg Library in Harlem, which was curated by James Briggs Murray, who was the curator of their Moving Image and Recorded Sound Division, who was also an advisor, or maybe on the initial Board of the Jazz Foundation of America
Yes. He was involved in the first conversation that allowed it to go from the Museum to the Jazz Foundation of America.
Now, I don’t know if we’re equipped to discuss how the Jazz Museum turned into the inspiration for...
Oh, I can tell you that.
Tell us, and give us some of the history of how the Jazz Foundation of America reached the point where you became its steward.
